plain: To bring a cost or penalty on oneself

webster.text: Literally, to run against; hence, to become liable to; to become subject to.

more.text: To bring on; as, to incur a debt; to incur guilt; to incur the displeasure of God; to incur blame or censure.
To occur; to meet; to press on.

example.quote: Can you suppose such a disposition in one of your citizens, as that, to oppress another man, he will incur greit expenses ?
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 20, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
